title: Replace brake pads
summary: Swap worn friction pads on one axle. Always do both sides of an axle together.
interval: Inspect at every service. Replace once friction material is below 3 mm, or sooner if worn unevenly.

options.label: Which axle?
options.note: Rear calipers vary far more than fronts. Tell us the axle for accurate steps.

safety: Never work under a car supported only by a jack. Use axle stands on a hard, level surface.
Brake dust may contain irritants. Do not blow it off with an airline; wipe it with brake cleaner and a rag.
Brakes are safety-critical. If anything does not go back exactly as it came off, stop and get it checked before driving.

tools.name: Torque wrench
tools.note: Guessing caliper and wheel torque is how wheels come off.

tools.name: Piston compression tool or large G-clamp
Copper or ceramic brake grease
tools.note: For slide pins and pad backing plates only. Never on the friction surface.

steps.title: Park and secure the car
steps.detail: Level, solid ground. Engine off, in gear (or P), handbrake on. Chock the wheels on the axle you are NOT lifting.

steps.title: Crack the wheel nuts while it is on the ground
steps.detail: Quarter-turn each, no more. Doing this in the air just spins the wheel.

steps.title: Jack up and support on axle stands
steps.detail: Use the manufacturer's jacking points. Lower the car onto the stands and give it a firm shove before you go near it.
steps.warning: A jack is a lifting device, not a supporting device.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and inspect
steps.detail: Check pad thickness, disc surface, and look for split flexi hoses or leaking caliper seals. A lipped or scored disc means discs as well as pads.

steps.title: Unbolt the caliper
steps.detail: Undo the slider bolts and swing or lift the caliper clear of the disc.
steps.warning: Support the caliper on an axle stand or hang it with wire. Letting it dangle on the brake hose damages the hose internally.

steps.title: Remove the old pads
steps.detail: Note the orientation, any anti-rattle shims, and whether a wear sensor is clipped into the inner pad. Photograph it before it all comes apart.

steps.title: Clean and grease the carrier
steps.detail: Wire-brush rust off the pad abutment surfaces so the new pads slide freely. Thin smear of brake grease on the slide pins and the pad backing plates.

steps.title: Retract the piston
steps.detail: Push the piston squarely back into the caliper with a piston tool or G-clamp against an old pad.
steps.warning: Fluid is pushed back up to the reservoir. Check the reservoir does not overflow, and never reuse fluid that has been pushed back if it is dirty.

steps.title: Fit the new pads and refit the caliper
steps.detail: New shims and clips if supplied. Refit the caliper and torque the bolts to spec — many are single-use and must be replaced.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and lower the car
steps.detail: Nuts finger-tight, lower onto the ground, then torque in a star pattern to spec.

steps.title: Pump the brake pedal before you move
steps.detail: Press the pedal repeatedly until it goes hard. This pushes the pistons back out to the discs.
steps.warning: Skip this and your first press of the pedal at the end of the driveway will go to the floor with no braking at all.

steps.title: Check the fluid level
steps.detail: Top up to MAX with the correct DOT specification if needed. Brake fluid strips paint — wipe spills immediately.

steps.title: Bed the pads in
steps.detail: Around ten moderate stops from 30 mph with cooling time between, then avoid hard braking for the first 200 miles. Expect a little smell and dust at first.
